summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 2% to INR103 crore while EBITDA margin fell to 17.36% from about 24%, with management guiding 15% FY27 growth.
summary.overview: FY26 sales turnover was INR103 crore versus INR101 crore, up about 2% YoY, and PBT was about INR14 crore. EBITDA was INR18.38 crore (17.36% margin), down from roughly 24% a year earlier, which management attributed to about INR8 crore of below-raw-material-cost API seal supply and INR5 crore of spending on 14 international exhibitions. Roughly 916 Middle East and other API seals are secured or in execution, of which 686 are supplied, but commissioning has slipped about 6-9 months (7 months as of the call) due to the Middle East geopolitical situation. Operating cash flow stayed negative with inventory rising to about INR62 crore, and management pushed meaningful cash flow to FY28.

financial_highlights.change: margin 17.36% vs about 24% in prior year

segments.commentary: INR14.5 crore in FY26, of which INR8.3 crore was API seal projects (45 single and 76 double seals) and INR6.2 crore regular OEM business.

segments.commentary: INR36.25 crore in FY26: INR11.2 crore API projects (about 322 single and 142 double seals) and INR25.05 crore non-API.

segments.commentary: INR11.26 crore domestic and about INR1 crore export in FY26; management said end-user business has not kicked in as expected due to geopolitics.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 15%.
FY27 EBITDA margin targeted at 23-24%, helped by cutting international exhibitions from 14 to about 5 (saving about INR3.5-4 crore) and tapering below-cost API seal subsidies.
Around 300-350 new API seals expected in FY27, already quoted, versus roughly 300 in the Middle East and 322 in India in FY26.
Replacement (aftermarket) spare-part business expected at about 80% gross margin; management said it cannot give an accurate FY27 picture given Middle East delays.
Operating cash flow expected to start improving in FY27, with FY28 seen as the better year to judge cash flow.
Commissioning of about 700 supplied seals assumed to start from 1 April 2027 in the base case, with replacement revenue earlier estimated around INR15 crore.
capex_capacity: Third manufacturing unit expansion is under way (mentioned by MD, no capex amount or commissioning date given).
Nuclear seal quotes active for Kudankulam expansion; management said nuclear order cycle is 2-3 years to order, 2 years to execute, and 1-2 years to commission.
Management said Middle East plants have not been impacted and plans to add service centres in Oman, Kuwait remain on track.
Possible need for external capital (debt or other means) if API subsidy-led order intake scales up, per MD.
demand_pricing: Middle East API seals: about 916 secured or in execution across UAE, Saudi, Oman, Kuwait and Iraq; 686 supplied and about 230 under execution. Management said about 20% of the 686 are now in commissioning, slowly.
Mongol project: about 118 seals supplied and 53 under execution, with more shipments expected by year-end.
India API seals: about 300 seals cited in India projects; installations reported at IOCL Panipat, Mathura, Barauni, Digboi and Talcher Fertilizers.
Pricing: management said Middle East realisation is about 1.25x India for the same seal; a thumb-rule value of about USD10,000 per seal (single about USD7,000, double USD12,000-14,000) was given.
Order book per management is better in June 2026 than June 2025.
Russia: management said Western exits have opened space for Sealmatic; described Russia as a good market.
Defence and marine (naval seals, submarine orders) and thermal power 660/800 MW projects cited as pipeline; management described these as slow-moving.

qa_highlights.question: How many of the 490-plus API seals supplied in 2025 are commissioned, and what is the replacement revenue progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Firoz gave the current count of 916 secured, 686 supplied and about 230 under execution. Management said commissioning was deferred 6-9 months by the Middle East situation, and FY27 numbers cannot be given precisely.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of commissioned seals in the 686 supplied?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated about 20% are in commissioning at a slow pace, with about 70% of the rest expected to commission once the Middle East situation settles.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth and margins are expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided about 15% revenue growth and EBITDA margin of 23-24%, citing lower exhibition spend and reduced below-cost API subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory high and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Delayed execution and China rare-earth export restrictions led to stopping some items, raising inventory to about INR62 crore. Management said cash flow would start improving in FY27, with FY28 a better year to judge.

qa_highlights.question: How much delay are end customers showing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said delays were about 7 months as of the call, mainly in the Middle East, while new Middle East project plans for the next five years continue.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need additional capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more API subsidy-led orders could require capital via debt or other means, but gave no specific plan.

risks_watch: Middle East commissioning delays (about 7 months as of the call) could push aftermarket revenue beyond FY27.
Below-cost API seal subsidies compress margins, and management said taking too many API orders would erode margins and cash flow.
Negative operating cash flow and INR62 crore inventory; watch for inventory reduction and cash flow turning positive in FY27-FY28.
Management gave no quantified FY27 replacement revenue and said it cannot give an accurate FY27 picture for the spare-part business.
Rare-earth supply restrictions from China cited as a reason for holding inventory.
Unhedged USD exposure; management said dollar moves cut both ways on realisations and imports.
Possible need for external debt or capital if API subsidy-led growth scales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term Middle East and nuclear opportunity and on margin recovery, but cautious and evasive on FY27 timing, commissioning schedules and quantified replacement revenue, repeatedly saying numbers cannot be given until site data is available.
